items.titleEn: Gold falls below $4,100, silver plunges 6% as hot CPI boosts Fed-hike bets - Kitco PM Report
items.summaryEn: (Kitco NewsWire) - Gold and silver prices were sharply lower in late U.S. trading Wednesday, as hotter-than-expected U.S. consumer inflation lifted Treasury yields, strengthened the dollar and increased expectations for further Federal Reserve tightening. Silver suffered particularly heavy losses as selling accelerated across precious metals. At the time of writing, spot gold was trading near $4,098.80 an ounce, down $61.30, or 1.47%, while spot silver was trading near $55.410, down $3.640, or 6.16%. North American equities closed sharply lower as the inflation report triggered selling in technology and other rate-sensitive shares. The S&P 500 dropped 86.51 points, or 1.1%, to 7,718.94, its worst daily performance since July. The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 48.62 points, or 0.1%, to 51,621.48. The Nasdaq Composite sank 511.51 points, or 1.9%, to 26,692.87, while the Russell 2000 declined 53.84 points, or 1.9%, to 2,729.53. European equities closed mostly higher, outperforming Wall Street as strong corporate earnings helped offset the U.S. inflation surprise. The Stoxx Europe 600 gained 0.43% to 637.75, supported by a 2.3% advance in health care shares and stronger semiconductor-equipment demand. Germany's DAX added 0.2% to 25,298.61, France's CAC 40 climbed 0.6% to 7,873.11 and the U.K. FTSE 100 rose 0.7% to 10,724.86. Italy's FTSE MIB bucked the regional advance, falling 0.61% to 49,753.84.

items.titleEn: Gold's weakness is a buying opportunity as Jefferies sees $5,000 price in 2027, healthy mining margins
items.summaryEn: (Kitco News) - Gold prices continue to struggle in the face of persistent inflation pressures and growing expectations for higher interest rates; however, one bank continues to see short-term weakness as a buying opportunity and expects higher gold prices to continue to support the mining sector. Despite rising energy costs, market analysts at Jefferies said they expect the mining sector's third-quarter earnings season to be "okay," as input cost pressures have remained relatively manageable. In their latest metals and mining report, published Friday, the analysts said that although higher bond yields have created significant headwinds for gold, they remain bullish on the precious metal over the longer term, and expect to see higher prices through next year.

Can gold hold $4,000 with an October rate hike still in play?
items.summaryEn: (Kitco News) - Hotter-than-expected consumer prices have put an October rate hike back in play , pushing real bond yields higher and dragging gold prices below a critical near-term support level. However, commodity analysts expect support to continue to hold at $4,000 an ounce, as the Federal Reserve is unlikely to raise interest rates just one week before American voters head to the polls for the 2026 midterm elections. In a note Wednesday, Ryan McKay, Director of Commodity Strategy at TD Securities, noted that gold’s inability to break through resistance at $4,200 has prompted speculative fund managers to liquidate their long positions, while the disappointing inflation numbers have added fuel to the fire.
